findings.problem: The first goal, 'Explain why no single cell can heal a cut finger alone', is shown before the Predict slide. It states the answer to the Predict question ('are these cells acting alone, or part of something bigger?'). The third goal, 'Compare the levels with a Kenyan school', also announces 'levels' and the school analogy before learners predict or meet Side B. The build log says the goals avoid giving away the discovery, which is not true. The lesson one-liner ('No single cell heals a cut finger alone') leaks the same result if it appears on the title slide.
findings.fix: Reword the goals so they do not state the result. For example: 'Predict and test what exists above a single cell', 'Build a hierarchy diagram using wound-healing examples', 'Use a school example to help explain your diagram'. Keep the 'no single cell' claim for the Explain and DQB slides, and keep it off the title slide.

findings.problem: The notes tell the teacher 'Do not name the levels yet', but the first SAY line starts 'Epithelial tissue: what do the school analogy and the microscope image have in common?'. This names the tissue level. The slide's third question ('How do different groups join to make skin?') also names 'skin'. The same SAY line is repeated on the next slide (hierarchy).
findings.fix: Make the SAY line match the SoW wording but remove the level name here, for example 'What do the school picture and the microscope image have in common?'. Say 'epithelial tissue' only on the hierarchy slide, and avoid repeating the question word for word.

findings.problem: The hero is a school compound, shown from the start of the lesson. It previews the school-analogy comparison that learners are meant to meet on Side B of the cards in Observe. It is reused as an illustration on the Evidence Card Set 10 slide, where it can be read as the real Side B card.
findings.fix: Use a neutral hero, such as the healing finger or the cell model. Use the school scene only after learners have filled in the table, or drop the repeat on the Evidence Card slide.

findings.problem: The SoW scissors reminder (cut away from the body, scissors flat on the desk, supervise cutting) is not written out anywhere on the deck. before_class only says 'read the reminder in the build log', and teachers do not read the build log.
findings.fix: Put the one-line scissors reminder directly in before_class and in the Observe notes, marked 'only if cutting cards'.

findings.problem: The fallback says 'Use the ARES video only as a last resort', but the hierarchy slide offers explain.video as an optional preview-first resource. The two instructions differ.
findings.fix: Make the wording the same: the video is optional, to be previewed first and used only after learners have built the hierarchy.

findings.slide: Think bigger: what is above a single cell? / Your turn: complete the Observation Table
findings.problem: For the SoW owner: the SoW has four biological images but five school levels, and the mastery check says '3 of 4 levels', so the table row count is unclear. It also expects learners to have Version 3 drawings of platelets, neutrophils and fibroblasts, which earlier lessons do not clearly produce. It also places all four cells under epithelial tissue. The build log flags these. The deck follows the SoW and tiles replace the projected cell drawings.
findings.fix: No deck change. Pass these points to the SoW owner, as the build log already does.

build_log.sow_says: A Form 1 student in Nairobi cuts their finger (unit phenomenon); 'one Form 2 student at Mwangaza Secondary School, Nairobi'; 'Form 2 Class of 42 students'
build_log.deck_does: Slides say 'student' and 'class of 42 students'. The Form 1 / Form 2 wording stays only in the SoW, not on slides. Notes say 'the student in Nairobi'.
build_log.why: CBE uses Grade, not Form. The SoW terms should be updated by the SoW owner.

build_log.sow_says: Lesson header 'Sub-Strand 1.1: Cell Structure'; unit data says 'Sub-Strand 1.3: Cell Structure and Specialisation'
build_log.deck_does: Uses no sub-strand number on Part A slides.
build_log.why: The sub-strand number does not match between the lesson and the unit data.

build_log.slide: Think bigger: what is above a single cell?
build_log.sow_says: four labelled cells from the wound-healing phenomenon (platelet, neutrophil, fibroblast, epidermal cell — drawings from their own Version 3 models)
build_log.deck_does: Shows the four cell names as tiles and asks learners to use their Version 3 drawings.
build_log.why: Lessons 3 to 9 do not clearly have learners draw platelets, neutrophils or fibroblasts in Versions 1 to 3 (Lesson 8 lists red and white blood cells, nerve, sperm and muscle cells). Learners may have no such drawings. The SoW owner should check.

build_log.slide: Your turn: complete the Observation Table
build_log.sow_says: Side A has four images ending at the integumentary system in a body outline; the Observation Table has 'Level of Organisation | Biological Example | School Analogy | Function' while Side B has five school levels, and the mastery threshold is '3 of 4 levels'
build_log.deck_does: Table has five rows (cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism). Answer key row 5 uses the whole human body, which is shown only as the body outline in image 4. Mastery check stays '3 of 4 biological levels'.
build_log.why: Five school levels and four biological images do not match. The SoW owner should say how many rows the table has.

build_log.slide: Your turn: complete the Observation Table
build_log.sow_says: skin as an organ (epidermis + dermis + hypodermis layers labelled)
build_log.deck_does: Keeps the three layers in the answer key as the SoW says.
build_log.why: Many textbooks describe the skin as epidermis and dermis, with the hypodermis as the tissue below the skin. A teacher should check.

build_log.sow_says: showing the four wound-healing cell types (platelet, neutrophil, fibroblast, epidermal cell) nested inside epithelial tissue → skin → integumentary system → human body
build_log.deck_does: Shows the five levels and lists all four cells at the Cell level, as the SoW says.
build_log.why: Only epidermal cells form epithelial tissue. Platelets (cell fragments, not whole cells) and neutrophils are in blood, and fibroblasts are in connective tissue. A teacher should check.

build_log.slide: Build Version 4: nest your cells in the hierarchy
build_log.sow_says: the relevant tissue each belongs to
build_log.deck_does: Answer key says neutrophils belong to blood tissue and epidermal cells form epithelial tissue.
build_log.why: The SoW does not name the tissue for neutrophils. Blood tissue is a standard textbook fact. A teacher should verify.

build_log.sow_says: A parallel is drawn to a Kenyan secondary school: ... school (organ) → county education system (organ system) → Kenyan society (organism)
build_log.deck_does: Uses the same school mapping on every slide. Notes warn that a school is like an organ, not an organ.
build_log.why: The analogy has limits. The Teacher Reflection already names the risk of confusion.

build_log.slide: Explain it in your own words
build_log.sow_says: embeds NGSS Science and Engineering Practice 6; 'Claim-Evidence-Reasoning (CER) Writing'
build_log.deck_does: Uses Claim, Evidence and Reasoning on the slide. No NGSS wording on slides.
build_log.why: NGSS is a US framework. Kenyan CBE terms are preferred for learners and teachers.

build_log.sow_says: Predict 4 min silent + 90 s pair talk + cold call; Observe 15 min + 2 group shares; Explain 8 min writing; DQB 3 min; Model 12 min + 2 min revision (about 50 minutes in total)
build_log.deck_does: The deck has a 76-minute set of phase slides plus 4 minutes for unit map, goals and Summary Table. Short set-up and sharing steps added around the SoW activities so the 80-minute period is filled. No activity is cut.
build_log.why: The SoW times add up to much less than 80 minutes, so no trimming is needed. Extra minutes go to set-up, sharing and checking.

build_log.sow_says: ARES Evidence Card Set 10 — a two-sided printed or on-screen resource
build_log.deck_does: Refers to it as a teacher-provided printed or on-screen resource. It is not in the ARES resource list, so no link is used.
build_log.why: No key for Evidence Card Set 10 was given. Teachers need the card images, the 'Mwangaza Secondary School' diagram and the school-side labels.

build_log.sow_says: Groups of 4 ... Distribute Evidence Card Set 10
build_log.deck_does: Does not state numbers of sets, sticky notes, coloured pens or a blank hierarchy template per group.
build_log.why: The SoW gives no quantities. The teacher checker should confirm them.

build_log.sow_says: No ARES resource is named in the SoW framework for the Explain phase.
build_log.deck_does: Offers explain.video ('Cells and organisms') as an optional preview-first resource on the hierarchy slide.
build_log.why: It is a US Khan Academy video and may not match the lesson exactly. Teacher should preview first.

build_log.slide: Think bigger: what is above a single cell?
build_log.sow_says: Image slides (the Predict slide shows four labelled cells)
build_log.deck_does: Uses icon tiles with cell names instead of drawings, because the cell drawings are in learners' own Version 3 models.
build_log.why: There is no diagram template for platelets, neutrophils or fibroblasts, and no new drawings were invented.

build_log.sow_says: Illustration use
build_log.deck_does: Uses three illustrations in Part A: hero school scene (new art_id school_compound_organisation, also reused on the Evidence Card Set 10 slide) and amina_healing_finger on the predictions slide. Part B may add more.
build_log.why: The Driving Question Board slide has no illustration to keep it from being too full.

build_log.sow_says: No hazardous materials are used in this lesson. If learners use scissors to cut diagram cards, remind them to cut away from the body and to place scissors flat on the desk when not in use.
build_log.deck_does: No Safety slide, because no practical or demonstration is done. The scissors reminder is only in before_class for the teacher.
build_log.why: The framework has no cutting activity, so the scissors line applies only if a teacher chooses to cut the cards. The teacher checker should confirm.

build_log.sow_says: Each learner receives two sticky notes; Evidence Card Set 10; groups of 4
build_log.deck_does: Lists materials with quantities only where the SoW gives them: two sticky notes per learner, one card set per group of 4.
build_log.why: The SoW gives no numbers for pens, templates, prompt cards or notebooks, so none were invented.

build_log.sow_says: ARES keys: predict.video, predict.reading, observe.reading, explain.reading, dqb.video, model.video (no resource named in the SoW framework)
build_log.deck_does: Marks these six as do_not_use and only explain.video as preview_first. No link is placed on any other slide.
build_log.why: They are US or off-topic resources: respiratory and digestive organs, cell differentiation, general biology. Several would give away the levels before learners predict or find them.

build_log.sow_says: ARES keywords: cell organisation, tissue, organ, organ system, organism, epithelial tissue, integumentary system, hierarchy
build_log.deck_does: Key words are hierarchy, organisation, analogy and model. The level names tissue, organ, organ system and organism are left for the Explain slides.
build_log.why: Key words are shown before Predict, so they must not answer the Predict question or give away the discovery.

build_log.sow_says: Lesson titles 1 to 12 of the sub-strand
build_log.deck_does: Uses short titles built only from words in each SoW lesson title. Lesson 6 appears as 'Observing Onion Epidermal Cells' and lesson 7 as 'Human Cheek Cells'.
build_log.why: The titles must stay within the SoW wording and fit the unit map layout.

build_log.sow_says: Kenyan school analogy diagram (student → class → Mwangaza Secondary School → Nairobi County Education → Kenyan society); 'Form 1 student'
build_log.deck_does: The summary answers say 'student' and 'school'. They do not use the Form 1 or Form 2 wording.
build_log.why: CBE uses Grade, not Form. The SoW owner should update the wording.
